summary: I built nothing, and the working tree is unchanged. The M5 and O-004 dispositions stop build from writing the cancel guard until risk-spike re-runs the cloud-placeholder cancel experiment with the scanner's real listing call. Spike 2 used a FindFirstFileExW stand-in, and the risk-spike stage has no attempt since the critique-review. I raised that as an obligation naming risk-spike (O-023) and listed the exact calls it must measure. I also ran the baseline build and the full test suite unchanged to confirm the starting point: the build is clean and all 86 tests pass.

payload.reason: The design is only accepted if a risk-spike measurement comes back as a go, and that measurement has not been taken. M5 was accepted, and its disposition says: "Before build writes the cancel guard, re-run spike 2's harness with the scanner's real listing call ... This measurement belongs to the spike, not to build. If it does not [free the call] ... the design is redone before build." O-004's discharge says: "The slice goes back to risk-spike for one experiment before build starts. If build is reached first, its first act is to raise an obligation naming risk-spike. It must not write ..." (the rest of that text is clipped). O-023 says: "Design is accepted only on a go." Build was reached first. In .taad/slices/SL-024/index.json the risk-spike stage has no attempt after critique-review (16:29:59Z), and the only cloud experiment on record is spike 2. That spike's own evidence says it used stand-ins ("FindFirstFileExW(FindExInfoBasic, LARGE_FETCH) ... I could not identify the Core scanner's real enumeration call, so these are stand-ins"). The scanner's real listing call is Kernel32.GetFileInformationByHandleEx on a CreateFileW(FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY, FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS) directory handle. Its info class is FileIdExtdDirectoryRestartInfo=20, then FileIdExtdDirectoryInfo=19. The fallback is FileFullDirectoryRestartInfo=15, then 14. It runs over a 64 KiB buffer (src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/DirectoryReader.cs:66, :96, :101, :113). If CancelSynchronousIo cannot free that call on a populating placeholder, the design's own fallback (abandon the thread, or run the scanner in its own process) replaces the in-place guard. Anything written now would then be discarded. So I am raising this on risk-spike and have left src/, tests/ and docs/ untouched. This does not need an administrator. Spike 2 registered and connected its sync root unelevated with hr=0. A builder should not stand up a cloud sync root on this machine anyway, because it registers a sync root in the user's settings. The disposition assigns the measurement to risk-spike.

obligations.how: RAISED ON risk-spike. Re-run cloud-fetch-placeholders-cancel with the same harness as spike 2: a never-answering provider in a separate process, CfRegisterSyncRoot with DISABLE_ON_DEMAND_POPULATION_ON_ROOT (2), and a placeholder directory left on on-demand population. Swap the FindFirstFileExW/Directory.Enumerate stand-in for the scanner's own calls. The open is CreateFileW(\\?\ path, FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY=0x1, share all, OPEN_EXISTING, FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS=0x02000000) (DirectoryReader.cs:66). The listing is GetFileInformationByHandleEx with FileIdExtdDirectoryRestartInfo=20 into a 64 KiB buffer, then FileIdExtdDirectoryInfo=19 (DirectoryReader.cs:96-113). Also run the fallback classes, FileFullDirectoryRestartInfo=15 then 14. Cancel from another thread with CancelSynchronousIo on an OpenThread(THREAD_TERMINATE) handle, repeated every 25 ms until the call returns. Record four things: which call blocks, whether it returns within 2 s of the first cancel, what it returns (995, SUCCESS with an empty or partial buffer, or a cloud error code), and how long CloseHandle takes afterwards. My evidence that this has not happened yet: index.json shows no risk-spike attempt after critique-review, and spike 2's own evidence says its calls were stand-ins. The design is accepted only on a go, so I wrote no guard.

Baseline on the unchanged tree: 86 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, exit 0. None of these tests exercises SL-024 behaviour, because none was built.

not_built: All of the design. That covers SynchronousIoCancel.cs, the additions to Kernel32 (995, THREAD_TERMINATE, GetCurrentThreadId, OpenThread, CancelSynchronousIo, SafeThreadHandle), the guarded DirectoryReader.Open/List, the guarded SizeProbe.Probe, and Scanner owning the guard with ClassifyReadError. It also covers SynchronousIoCancelTests, the additions to CancellationTests, and the replacement for the deferral note at docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:101. The M5 and O-004 dispositions say build must not write the cancel guard before risk-spike measures the scanner's real GetFileInformationByHandleEx call on a populating cloud placeholder. That measurement has not been taken, and a no-go would replace the in-place guard with the design's fallback.
follow_ups: risk-spike should also record the CloseHandle latency on the placeholder directory handle after the cancelled listing. That is the cloud counterpart of O-003, and it is cheap to take in the same run.

O-004's discharge text reached this build clipped at "It must not write". The engine should hand the full disposition to build-slice so the constraint does not have to be reconstructed from the M5 disposition.

The design's open question on spike 3 (a stalled, established SMB session) still needs a person. The options are a Defender exclusion for the spike venv, or approval of a different unelevated SMB2 target on port 4450. Until it is answered, O-003 and O-018 cannot be discharged by measurement.
